entries.subject: Radius, mass and temperature
entries.finding: Limbach et al. (2025), Table 1: radius 0.0121 +/- 0.0002 solar radii, mass 0.605 +/- 0.013 solar masses, effective temperature 4920 +/- 50 K. They supersede Vanderburg et al. (2020), Table 1 (0.0131 solar radii, 0.518 solar masses, 4710 K). The display axis is sky north, not a measured pole.

entries.subject: Photosphere colour
entries.finding: Gaia DR3 publishes only the continuous BP/RP coefficients for source 2146576589564898688 (has_xp_sampled = false). They are sampled on the archive grid with GaiaXPy 2.1.4 (tools/objects/observation/xp-continuous-sample.py), as for TRAPPIST-1. Signal-to-noise is 2 at 380 nm and 17 to 34 from 500 to 780 nm.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The only law fitted to this star's transits, Gendreau-Distler et al. (2026), Table 1 (Bessel R, stacked light curve), gives u1 = 0.52 +/- 0.32 and u2 = 0.52 +/- 0.34. The limb intensity 1 - u1 - u2 = -0.04 is below zero, which the shared limb preparer refuses. The transit is grazing, so it samples only part of the limb. The disc is drawn uniform.
entries.revisitWhen: A published limb-darkening law for this white dwarf keeps the limb between dark and the centre brightness.

entries.subject: Radial velocity
entries.finding: The white dwarf's featureless spectrum gives no radial velocity. The record uses the mean of Gaia DR3's values for its co-moving companions G 229-20 A (17.19 +/- 0.33 km/s) and B (17.38 +/- 0.35 km/s): 17.29 km/s, a derived value. It moves the star by far less than a pixel over the scene's time range.

entries.subject: Wide companions G 229-20 A and B
entries.finding: Vanderburg et al. (2020) identify WD 1856+534 as the distant third member of a triple with the M-dwarf pair G 229-20 A/B, about 43 arcseconds away. This package shows the white dwarf and its planet only.
entries.revisitWhen: The M-dwarf pair is prepared as star packages bound to this system.
